description: Look up the geologic time scale — eons, eras, periods, epochs, and ages with their absolute-age boundaries in millions of years (Ma) and nesting. This is the reference that grounds every temporal filter on the other tools and translates a named interval like "Late Cretaceous" to its 100.5–66.0 Ma boundaries (and back). Filter by a name substring, a Ma range (overlap match), and/or a level; call with no filters to browse the full scale. Browsing and every name on the bundled ICS international-scale snapshot are answered offline. A name the snapshot does not carry — the sub-stage and regional names that occurrence and collection rows report, such as "Late Maastrichtian" or "Lancian" — costs one PBDB lookup across its other time scales; the response names which source answered and which scale the interval belongs to.

level.description: Restrict to one rank of the international scale: eon, era, period, epoch, or age (finest). Browsing is bounded to that scale, so the sub-stage and regional ranks are not selectable here.

max_ma.description: Older bound of an age window (Ma); intervals overlapping [min_ma, max_ma] match.

min_ma.description: Younger bound of an age window (Ma); intervals overlapping [min_ma, max_ma] match.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring of the interval name, e.g. "cretaceous" or "Jurassic". A name the bundled international scale does not carry is matched exactly against PBDB's other time scales.

name: paleobiology_list_intervals

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `interval_not_found`: A named interval filter matched nothing — neither the bundled international scale (after any level or Ma filters) nor a PBDB lookup across its other time scales. `interval_lookup_unavailable`: The name is outside the bundled international scale and the PBDB lookup that covers the other time scales could not be reached. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

items.description: A geologic time interval with its rank, Ma boundaries, and parent.

abbrev.description: Standard abbreviation (e.g. "K" for Cretaceous), when defined.

color.description: ICS chart hex color for this interval, when defined.

interval_no.description: PBDB interval id for this geologic interval.

level.description: Rank of the interval in its time scale. The international scale uses eon > era > period > epoch > age (finest); other PBDB scales also use subepoch, subage, zone, subzone, chron, subchron, and bin.

max_ma.description: Older (bottom) boundary in millions of years ago.

min_ma.description: Younger (top) boundary in millions of years ago.

parent_no.description: PBDB id of the containing interval (epoch→period→era→eon). Omitted at the top.

scale.description: The PBDB time scale carrying this interval, e.g. "Mesozoic Subages" or "North American Land Mammal Ages". Present only on an interval resolved upstream — every bundled interval is on the international scale, which snapshot_version names.

notice.description: Guidance when no interval matched the filters.

snapshot_version.description: ICS chart version and generation date of the bundled time scale, for citation.

source.description: Which source answered: "bundled_ics" for the offline international-scale snapshot, "pbdb_upstream" for a name resolved live against PBDB's other time scales.

totalCount.description: Number of intervals matched by the filters.

title: paleobiology-mcp-server: list geologic intervals
